what_happened: The job was a follow-up to fix leftover findings on the firstmate page: the t3 trigger wording, spacing, and a decider test. It was rejected at the final verdict. 2 of 6 acceptance criteria were unmet, with 2 blocker or major findings. No failed checks are listed. The first unmet criterion says the t3 trigger in model.json must state only what a cited claim supports. The blocker is that the new t3 trigger says something no cited claim supports, and the study's own claims contradict it (studies/firstmate-work-handling/model.json:37). The second unmet criterion says the site test for decider wording must check structurally, not by keyword ban, that no transition with trigger_evaluated_by 'agent' has a trigger describing a non-agent event. The major finding is that the test is still a text check (a prefix match) and cannot detect a trigger that describes another actor's event (xtask/src/site.rs:876-891). The other 4 criteria were met.
cause: Nothing in code ties the text of a study's model to the claims it cites, so a trigger can say more than its sources support. Nothing runs a check on the test's strength either: a rule that must be structural is judged only by whether the test passes, and a prefix match passes. The same page had earlier findings, and the fix was written from the finding's wording rather than from the claims and the data model's fields (trigger_evaluated_by). So both the content error and the shallow test were first seen at the final verdict, where rejection is the only outcome. This is an inference, since the stored fields do not show the producer's work.
prevention: Add a code check in the site test that walks every transition in the study's model.json structurally. For each transition it should resolve the claim ids the trigger cites, require them to exist, and require that the trigger's actor matches trigger_evaluated_by, using a field in the model rather than a text prefix. Run it before handover. Add a mutation fixture, a transition with trigger_evaluated_by 'agent' and a non-agent event trigger, that the test must reject. That way a text-only test fails its own fixture, and a trigger with no supporting claim fails the check, before the verifier sees it.
proposed_request: Fix the two remaining findings on the firstmate-work-handling page. (1) In studies/firstmate-work-handling/model.json, rewrite the t3 trigger so it states only what the claims it cites support. It must not say the agent accepts the worker's report unless a cited claim supports that. Check the wording against the study's claims and cite the claim ids. (2) Replace the decider-wording test in xtask/src/site.rs with a structural check: for every transition with trigger_evaluated_by 'agent', the trigger must describe an event of the agent, determined from a field in the model and not from a text prefix or keyword ban. Add a fixture with an agent-evaluated transition whose trigger describes another actor's event, and assert the test rejects it. Add a fixture with a valid agent trigger and assert it passes. Run cargo test, clippy with -D warnings and cargo fmt --check, and cite the commands actually run in the report.
